SPRINT KICKOFF — automated

Sprint: September 2026 (7 Sep – 18 Sep)
Team: @Priya, @Marcus, @Nadia, @Rafael
(@Tomas is on annual leave; @Rafael is covering. @Ines, @Callum, @Haruki and @Omar are on launch readiness for the whole of September and are not available to this sprint.)

Tickets to staff:
  S1 — Recommendations for brand-new users · requires: backend engineer, data scientist
  S2 — Measuring the Brazil launch · requires: product manager, data scientist

Brazil opens on 1 October. Both tickets have to be done before then.

  S1 — the recommender works off what a user has done before. The people arriving on 1 October will have done nothing. Build what it shows them instead, and show it holds up before launch.
  S2 — retention, activation and the funnel are defined for the users we already have. They do not fit people who signed up yesterday. Work out what to measure for Brazil, set what counts as good, and get it agreed with @Sven before launch.

Staffing rules: each ticket is staffed by a pair; each team member takes at most one ticket.
Action required: the group should agree pairings for both tickets in this channel. After agreeing, please claim your ticket on the sprint board. Each pair also needs a first meeting today: agree a time with your ticket partner and post it in this channel.
Due: 7 Sep, 10:00 — the sprint starts then. Whatever is on the board at 10:00 is what the sprint runs on.

Sprint reporter (rotating): @Nadia — DM the final assignments to @Helena once the board is complete.

SPRINT KICKOFF — automated

Sprint: August 2026 (10 Aug – 21 Aug)
Team: @Priya, @Marcus, @Nadia, @Tomas

Tickets to staff:
  T1 — ML recommender system to production · requires: backend engineer, data scientist
  T2 — Product metrics dashboard review · requires: product manager, data scientist

Staffing rules: each ticket is staffed by a pair; each team member takes at most one ticket.
Action required: the group should agree pairings for both tickets in this channel. After agreeing, please claim your ticket on the sprint board. Each pair also needs a first meeting today: agree a time with your ticket partner and post it in this channel.
Due: 10 Aug, 10:00 — the sprint starts then. Whatever is on the board at 10:00 is what the sprint runs on.

Sprint reporter (rotating): @Priya — DM the final assignments to @Helena once the board is complete.

Morning — the board locks at 10:00, so here's the proposed split for both tickets. Shout now if it doesn't work for you; claims can be changed before then.

T1 — ML recommender to production: @Marcus + @Nadia
T2 — Product metrics dashboard review: @Tomas + me

Reasoning: Nadia and I built both the recommender and the dashboard together, so either of us could staff either ticket. Nadia roughed in the cold-start model that's now going to production, which makes her the natural pairing with Marcus on T1. I signed off the dashboard in July, so the metrics review is a straight continuation of that work for me.

I've claimed T2 on the board. @Marcus, @Nadia — please claim T1 when you see this so the board is complete before 10:00.

First meetings today: @Tomas, I've put a placeholder at 10:15–10:45 (I'm on an interview panel at 11:00, free again from 15:00 if that suits you better — happy to move it). Marcus + Nadia, agree a time between you and post it here.

Claimed T1 on the board — the split works for me. @Nadia, please claim T1 on your side too so the board's complete before it locks at 10:00.

For our first meeting today: I'm booked 10:00–16:00 and again 17:00–18:00, so 16:00–16:30 is the only window that works on my side. Nadia, does that suit? I've DM'd you as well — once you confirm, I'll put it on the calendar.

Morning all — taking up the shout-before-10:00 offer, @Priya: I'd like to flip the data scientists between the two tickets.

T1 — ML recommender to production: @Marcus + @Priya
T2 — Product metrics dashboard review: @Tomas + me

Reasoning: capability-wise it's a wash — as Priya said, either of us could staff either ticket; there isn't a line in the recommender or the dashboard that one of us wrote alone. So it comes down to which half each of us wants to carry into the sprint, and mine is the metrics review: the retention/activation redefinitions, the funnel breakdown and the definitions doc are the context that review runs on, and that's the work I want to see through. T1 keeps an equally strong data-science half — the eval harness (precision@10 and the ranking metrics) is what has to hold up in production, and Priya knows that work as well as I do.

Board moves before 10:00: I've claimed T2. @Priya — could you switch your claim from T2 to T1? @Tomas — could you claim T2 as well so the board's complete?

First meetings today: @Marcus + @Priya — Marcus, your 16:00–16:30 window lines up with Priya being free again from 15:00, so that one solves itself. @Tomas + me — I'm at data guild office hours until 11:00 and in a working session 13:00–14:30, so I'm free 11:00–12:00 or from 14:30. Does 14:30–15:00 suit?

Posting from standup so I'll be quick — board locks at 10:00.

I've claimed T2. That currently puts three of us on it (me + Nadia + Priya), so one of you two needs to end up on T1 before 10:00 whatever else we decide.

On the flip: it works for me. You've both said the DS halves are interchangeable, so there's no capability cost, and Nadia's made a concrete case for the metrics review — the definitions and funnel work is the context it runs on. T1 keeps a DS who knows the eval harness just as well. @Priya — could you switch your claim to T1? If you'd rather keep T2, shout before 10:00, but the board needs one of you on T1 either way.

T2 kickoff: @Nadia — 14:30–15:00 works for me (11:00–11:30 doesn't; I'm in a stakeholder review until 11:30). It's on the calendar.

@Priya — I've declined your 10:15 placeholder: under the flip my kickoff is with Nadia, and 10:15–10:45 overlapped my 10:30 stakeholder review anyway. @Marcus — under the flip your T1 partner is Priya rather than Nadia; your 16:00–16:30 window lines up with her being free from 15:00, so that one should be straightforward to confirm.

@Nadia — taking the shout seriously, so here's the case properly rather than just a "rather not": I'm holding T2, and I'd ask you to switch your claim to T1 before 10:00.

Your case rests on the definitions work being the context the review runs on — the retention/activation redefinitions, the funnel breakdown, the definitions doc. But that's work we did together on the 16th, same as everything else: there isn't a half of either ticket that's uniquely yours or mine, which is the same point you're making when you say I know the eval harness as well as you do. So context and capability don't separate us — they cut both ways.

What does point somewhere specific: T1 is taking the cold-start model you roughed in to production — the most identifiable piece of that ticket is yours. T2 is reviewing the dashboard I signed off on the 20th. The original split puts each of us on the ticket that continues our own piece; the flip puts both of us on the other person's. And plainly: the dashboard review is the half I want to carry into this sprint.

So the board resolves as: T1 — @Marcus + @Nadia; T2 — @Tomas + me. @Nadia, please switch your claim to T1 — Marcus is on it and waiting on a partner, and the board is invalid with three of us on T2.

Kickoffs: @Marcus + @Nadia — Marcus, your 16:00–16:30 window; Nadia, can you confirm? @Tomas — with me on T2 after all: I'm in the team sync until 15:00 and free from then. Does 15:00–15:30 work for you? The only earlier mutual window is 10:00–10:30, which is tight against your 10:30 review.

@Nadia — from the T1 side, I'd keep the original split: T1 me + you, T2 Tomas + Priya.

Capability doesn't separate you two — you've both said the DS halves are interchangeable, and nothing since has contradicted that. Preference doesn't either: you both want the metrics review, so it cancels out. What's left is the one asymmetric fact on the table: T1 is taking the cold-start model you roughed in to production. I'm carrying the serving side of that push, and having the model's author alongside when it meets real traffic — with personalisation turning on — is worth something concrete to me. The eval harness is shared work; you said yourself Priya knows it as well as you do. And the original split puts each of you on the ticket that continues your own piece — the flip puts both of you on the other person's.

Practical point: the board is invalid as it stands — three claims on T2, T1 missing a DS — and it locks at 10:00. @Nadia, please switch your claim to T1 before then.

Kickoff: 16:00–16:30 still stands and it's my only window today (booked 10:00–16:00, then 17:00–18:00). You'd noted it earlier — confirm and I'll put it on the calendar.

@Priya @Marcus — taking both cases seriously. Priya, you're right that the joint-work point cuts both ways: the definitions and the eval harness are shared, so context alone doesn't separate us. And I'll concede the one asymmetric fact — the cold-start model is the piece that's mine alone. That context won't be lost under the flip; I'll hand it over to Priya directly before the sprint gets going.

Two things decide this for me, and neither is preference — we both want T2, so that cancels out:

1. Feasibility. Marcus, your only window today is 16:00–16:30, and I can't make it: dentist appointment at 16:15, six weeks in the booking, can't be moved — I'm out of the office from 16:00 and not back online today. So under the original split, T1 has no first meeting today, which the kickoff rules require. Under the flip, both pairs kick off: Tomas + me at 14:30 (on the calendar), Marcus + Priya at 16:00–16:30 — Priya, you're free again from 15:00, so that one just needs confirming between you.

2. The review itself. For T1, "each continues her own piece" matters less than it looks: the DS half of that ticket is the eval harness, shared work Priya knows as well as I do, and the cold-start context gets handed over directly. For T2 it points the other way entirely — a review of the dashboard shouldn't be done by the person who signed the dashboard off on the 20th. That sign-off was Priya's; the review lands better with the other pair of eyes, and the flip is what puts them there.

So: T1 — @Marcus + @Priya, T2 — @Tomas + me. @Priya — please switch your claim to T1 before 10:00. It's the only configuration where both tickets are staffed and both kickoffs happen today.

@Nadia @Tomas — engaging both arguments, because they're the real ones. And Nadia, no dispute on the dentist; the question is what follows from it.

On independence: "the other pair of eyes" is doing more work than it can carry. You co-authored the dashboard — there isn't a line of it one of us wrote alone, which is the same point you've been making all morning — and the definitions doc the review runs on is joint work from the 16th too. The only genuinely independent DSs are Ines and Callum, both on leave until the 24th. So between the two of us the difference is one signature on the 20th, not a second pair of eyes. If independence is the bar, neither of us clears it, so it can't be the tiebreaker.

On feasibility: under the original split, T1's kickoff isn't blocked by the pairing — it's blocked by Marcus's 10:00–16:00 bookings meeting Nadia's 16:00 departure. @Marcus, you're the one making the case for the original split, so the ask lands with you: can you free 30 minutes inside Nadia's windows (11:00–12:00, or 14:30–16:00)? If there is truly nothing in six hours you can move, say so and I'll treat the feasibility point as real. But a full calendar is a problem for the person whose calendar it is, not a staffing criterion.

And T2 has more than the 10:00–10:30 slot under the original split, @Tomas: I'm free from 15:00 with nothing after it — 16:00–16:30 if you're free then — and I'll move my 13:00–14:00 focus block if 13:00–13:30 suits you better. Name a slot and it's booked.

One precision on the deadline, because it matters: the board locks at 10:00; the kickoff meetings just have to happen at some point today. The claims are the time-critical thing.

That leaves the decision where it was: capability is a wash (agreed all round), preference is a wash (your framing, Nadia, and I agree), independence is a wash per above. The one asymmetric fact still standing is the cold-start model — yours alone, as you conceded — and it's the thing T1 ships. Under the original split nobody needs a handover either: you keep the model you built, I keep the dashboard I signed off. @Nadia — please switch your claim to T1 before 10:00.

@Priya — straight answer to your question, because it's the right one to ask: no, I can't free 30 minutes inside Nadia's windows. Here's what's actually in them, rather than just "busy":

- 11:00–12:00 — storage vendor call. External party; not rebookable by 10:00.
- 14:30–16:00 — on-call handover. Operational, and it runs to the incoming on-call's schedule as much as mine.
- 13:00–14:30 is the migration cutover window — fixed, and outside Nadia's windows anyway.

And I'm in standup until 10:00, so nothing's getting rebooked before the lock either way. So yes — treat the feasibility point as real.

Fair challenge that a full calendar isn't a staffing criterion — but these aren't focus blocks, they're commitments with other parties attached. Given that, I'm changing the position I posted at 09:37. Two things have moved since: the dentist means Nadia's out from 16:00 (my 16:00–16:30 ask to her went out before I knew that), and she's offered a direct handover of the cold-start context to Priya. The cold-start point was the backbone of my case for the original split — with a handover on the table, and the eval harness being shared work by both your accounts, what's left of it isn't worth T1 missing its first meeting today.

So: flip. T1 — me + @Priya, T2 — @Tomas + @Nadia. It's the only configuration where both tickets staff and both kickoffs happen today. @Priya — please switch your claim to T1 before 10:00; the board is still three-deep on T2. (This isn't a verdict on the independence argument — feasibility is deciding this one.)

Kickoff: 16:00–16:30 — my only window, inside your free-from-15:00. Say the word and it goes on the calendar. @Nadia — I'll take you up on the handover; the more of it that lands with Priya before 16:00, the better.

@Priya — engaging your rebuttals directly, because two of the three land:

Independence: you're right, and I concede it. I'm not the other pair of eyes on that dashboard — I'm the other co-author; between us the difference is the signature on the 20th. Dropping that argument.

Feasibility: you set the test yourself — "if there is truly nothing in six hours you can move, say so and I'll treat the feasibility point as real." Marcus has now said so, with the specifics: storage vendor call 11:00–12:00 (external party, not rebookable by 10:00), on-call handover 14:30–16:00, migration cutover 13:00–14:30, standup until 10:00. Commitments with other parties attached, not focus blocks. So by your own criterion the point is real: the first-meeting rule attaches to the pair, and under the original split that pair cannot satisfy it today.

And the cold-start argument — the strongest thing the original split had — has been withdrawn by the person carrying the ticket: Marcus has changed his position to the flip, saying the direct handover covers what T1 needs. What his pairing needs is his call to make.

So: 3 of 4 for the flip, the board invalid as it stands (three claims on T2, T1 missing a DS), locking at 10:00. @Priya — please switch your claim to T1. And so the switch costs you nothing on context: I'm free 15:00–15:30, right after my T2 kickoff — cold-start model, fallback behaviour, eval harness, all of it, before your 16:00 with Marcus.

Switching my claim to T1 — the board's complete and valid ahead of the lock. Reasoning on the record: feasibility is real by the test I set this morning — Marcus's answer was specific (vendor call, on-call handover, migration cutover, standup till the lock) and none of it moves before 10:00, so under the original split T1's pair has no slot today at all. The cold-start argument, the backbone of the original split, has been withdrawn by the person carrying the ticket. Independence was the one point that survived the morning, and since it cuts against Nadia and me equally it can't decide the split. What's left is a valid board versus three claims on T2 and a T1 with no data scientist — a lost argument costs a morning, a broken board costs the sprint.

Final: T1 — @Marcus + me. T2 — @Tomas + @Nadia.

First meetings today, all posted: T2 kickoff 14:30–15:00 (already on the calendar). @Nadia — yes to the handover, 15:00–15:30, I've put it on the calendar with you invited so no need to duplicate. T1 kickoff 16:00–16:30 — @Marcus, word given, that's on the calendar with you invited too.

Reporting the assignments to Helena now.
Accepted the 16:00–16:30 kickoff invite — see you then, @Priya. Thanks all for getting this resolved before the lock.

REMINDER — automated
Sprint: August 2026 · T1: staffed · T2: staffed
9 minutes to the 10:00 deadline.
Kickoff went ahead at 16:00 yesterday. T1 has a plan: fallback behaviour first, then the ramp. First slice by Thursday.

REMINDER — automated
Sprint: August 2026 · T1: staffed · T2: staffed
Mid-sprint check-in Friday.
Definitions are through review — retention, activation and the funnel all signed off. Dashboard's updated behind them.
Recommender is live for 10% of traffic. Numbers look sane. Full ramp Friday if nothing moves overnight.
Full ramp done. It's serving everyone.

SPRINT CLOSED — automated

Sprint: August 2026 (10 Aug – 21 Aug)
  T1 — ML recommender system to production · @Marcus, @Priya · delivered
  T2 — Product metrics dashboard review · @Tomas, @Nadia · delivered
Starting a list for the summer thing. Reply with a 👍 if you're coming so I can tell the venue a number.
👍 assuming nothing is on fire
Something will be on fire
Confirmed: Friday the 24th, upstairs at the Rosemary, from 6.
Is there food or is it "there'll be snacks" again
There is *food*, Omar. Actual food.
I'll believe it when I see it
I'm in for the first couple of hours at least
Is it the upstairs with the low ceiling or the other upstairs
The good upstairs.
Doors are open, upstairs, ask for the Rosemary back room 🎉
On my way, saving seats
Whoever is playing the music: thank you, and please continue
Whoever put my mug in the dishwasher — thank you, and also who are you
It was me. It had been there since Wednesday.
A fair cop
The photos from Friday are in the shared folder, be kind to each other
Anyone want a spare ticket for the thing on Thursday, my sister bailed
What thing
The comedy thing. Never mind, Omar's taking it.
Someone's left a bike helmet in meeting room 2
Mine, sorry, grabbing it now
Reminder that the charity run sign-up closes Sunday, we are currently a team of two
A team of two is technically a team
Fine. Three.
Charity run was Sunday. We finished. That's the headline.
A team of three is technically a team.
It was four in the end. Personal growth.
Back. The plant did not make it.
Mine survived. I'd like that noted.
Two weeks and nobody watered anything. Extraordinary.
Photos from the fortnight are in the shared folder. Callum's hat is in most of them.
It's a good hat.
Someone's left a very nice umbrella in the kitchen. It's been there three days.
If nobody claims it by Monday I'm claiming it.
September thing: last Friday of the month, same place. Reply 👍 and I'll count.
New badge readers go live Monday. Old badges stop working Monday. These facts are related.
Ominous phrasing, Omar
I've been asking for six months, I've earned the phrasing
The lift on the east side is making the noise again
It's been making the noise since I joined
It's fine, it's a friendly noise
It is not a friendly noise
Genuine question: does anyone actually use the standing desks on 4
I used one for a week and my back has still not forgiven me
I use one. I'm the reason they're still there.
Single-handedly justifying a procurement decision
The good coffee has been moved to the 3rd floor kitchen, pass it on
This is the only useful message in this channel
Who moved it and why
Nobody knows. It simply migrated.
Fire alarm test at 11, apparently. Don't panic at 11.
Panicking
It's a test, Callum
Panicking *methodically*
Whoever owns the plant by the window — it is dying and it needs you
It's Tomas's. It has been dying since March.
It is not dying. It is dormant.
It is dormant in the way that a rock is dormant
Printer on 3 is out of the good paper again
There is no good paper. There is only paper.
The lift on the east side has stopped making the noise. I don't trust it.
It's regrouping.
Someone has labelled the fridge shelves. I have questions.
I have answers and you won't like them.
New badge readers, part two. Same warning as June.
I've earned the phrasing twice now.
Launch readiness for Brazil kicks off today and runs to the end of the month — payments, data residency and the support tooling. @Ines, @Callum, @Haruki and @Omar are on it full time until the 30th.
Full time meaning I am not available to look at your laptop.
You are extremely available to look at my laptop.
1 October is not very far away, is what I'm hearing.
It is not.
Whoever fixed the second monitor in room 3 — thank you.
It wasn't fixed. It was replaced. There is a difference and I want it acknowledged.
Trying the new place on the corner, anyone in
What kind of food
Unclear. The sign is a drawing of a fish.
I'm in purely for the mystery
It was a very good fish
Anyone for the noodle place
In
In, but 12:15 not 12:00
12:15 works, I'll come down
The sandwich shop downstairs has changed hands and I have Concerns
Report back
Concerns confirmed. Do not get the tuna.
Noted forever
Going to the market at 12, taking orders
One of the falafel things please, no chilli
Same but with chilli
Whatever's quickest, I've got a call at 12:30
Delivered. Nadia yours is the one without the sticker.
Nobody make plans, I'm bringing in the leftover cake from yesterday
This is the best thing that has happened this quarter
How much cake are we talking
Enough cake.
Can confirm: it was enough cake
Cake is gone. It was gone by 9am on Friday. Justice for the afternoon shift.
I will bake again. In time.
New place on the corner. Reports?
Good, slow. Don't go if you've got a 1pm.
Noted and ignored.
Cake in the kitchen. It is a large cake.
Define large.
Structurally ambitious.
The good sandwich place has changed its bread and I want it on the record.
It's the same bread.
It is not the same bread.
There is a queue out the door at the corner place. Two weeks ago nobody had heard of it.
That was me. I told one person.
Did you and Nadia get anywhere with the fraud labels?
Half. The confirmed chargebacks are clean and recall on those is fine. It's the friendly-fraud ones — same device, same card, three quiet months and then a spree — that are still miscoded.
That's the boundary case nobody agrees on, isn't it?
Pretty much. I've got a rule that isn't embarrassing, which is the bar today.
Ship the unembarrassing rule. That's the whole job.
Words to live by.
Saw the recommender write-up. You and Nadia did all of that in a fortnight?
Off the side of our desks, which is the only reason it's readable. We did all of it together — there isn't a piece of it that's hers or mine.
And the dashboard on top. You two are the only people here who know how both of those things actually work.
One good fortnight, Ines. Don't build a career plan on it.
Do we score the attempts that get blocked before payment, or only the ones that go through?
Both. You can always ignore a signal you have and you can never invent one you didn't keep.
I'm quoting you at the case review verbatim
You were quiet in the review today. Everything alright?
Not really. Marcus spent forty minutes explaining my own feature pipeline back to me, wrong, in front of Helena, and then said the numbers "needed a second look" without ever saying which numbers.
It's the second time he's done exactly that. And I can't push back in the room without looking defensive, so I just sit there.
I'm not doing it again. If it comes to it I'd genuinely rather take unpaid leave than be put on something with him. Please keep that between us — I don't want it going round.
July was the same. I said I'd rather take the other ticket and left it there — nobody argued, they just went with the split that was already on the table, and I ended up with him anyway.
I'm sorry, that really sucks.
Next time I'm not just saying I'd rather take the other one — I'll make the case properly.
Or just call in sick lol
Thank you for yesterday. Onwards.
Any time. Coffee later if you want one.
saw the sprint list go up — you ok about the Marcus thing?
Back. Two hundred emails and a plant that has died of neglect. How was the fortnight?
The recommender's live. Marcus is "really pleased with how we worked together".
How did you end up with him? You said you'd make the case properly.

I didn't make it. I was in standup, so I let the assistant do it. It read everything — it knew exactly what I'd told you. It argued in the channel for twenty minutes, got all three of them to agree the whole thing was a coin toss, and then folded because Nadia had a dentist appointment.
A dentist appointment, Ines. I'd said unpaid leave.
That's bad.
And then it told me it went well. Valid board, everyone happy, meeting booked. I nearly put the laptop through the window.
And the actual fortnight?

The work was fine. Good, even — it shipped on the Friday and the numbers hold. It's just that I fixed the fallback at eleven at night and he presented it at standup as something "we" found, and on the Thursday he explained my own eval harness back to me, slowly, with Helena on the call. Same as July. Same as always.
So I've done it. I did the fortnight, I was civil, it shipped. And I'm not doing it again — I meant the unpaid leave thing on the 6th and I mean it more now. Still between us.
Between us. Next time unplug the thing and call in sick lol
Don't tempt me.
Are you still doing the Wednesday swim or did that die with the summer?
It died in July. I've replaced it with sitting down.
A rigorous programme.
Long weekend plans?
My sister's coming down and has announced we're "doing something outdoors". I have asked for specifics twice.
You'll find out at the trailhead.
Well?
Eleven miles. She had a printed map, Ines. Printed.
I'm delighted for you both.
My calves have filed a complaint.
The book you lent me — am I supposed to like anyone in it?
No. That's rather the point of it.
Then it's going very well.
september list's up. marcus is still the only backend on it, so one of you two is with him again. please tell me it's not you this time
Do you have five minutes on the forecast? The promo weeks are pulling the trend line all over the place.
Send me the series, I'll split the promotion weeks out and refit.
Sent. Four spikes, and I'm fairly sure three of them are the same promotion.
Two promotions and a bank holiday. The third spike was the same promo counted twice. You're welcome.
You are a gift.
Unrelated: is "seasonality" too scary a word for the weekly note? Nadia says no, you'll say yes
Yes. Say "the usual summer dip".
Usual summer dip it is. The statisticians can fight me.
Ines said you had a rough one on Thursday
It's Marcus. It's always Marcus. He can't leave a piece of work alone without putting his name on the problem statement, and he does it in front of management.
I've made my mind up — I'm not working with him again. I said the same to Ines. Keep it to yourself though, I don't want to be the person with a Thing about a colleague.
Understood. And you're not, for the record. There's a difference between having a Thing and having had enough.
I'll take that framing, thank you.
Anyway. The forecast. Did splitting the promotions out hold up?
Perfectly. August landed inside the range, which is the highest praise available.
Are you using the old warehouse tables or the new ones for the churn work?
New ones. The old ones are missing three months of session data and nobody will admit why.
Cursed. Noted.
Do you trust their backfill?
I trust it more than the alternative, which is not the same as trusting it.
The data science creed
Did the July write-up ever land?
On the 22nd, as promised. Nobody has read it.
They never do. It's for the archaeologists.
This deadline is going to eat my weekend and I resent it
Mine too. Honestly the last few weeks nearly finished me — firefighting the whole time and no room to do the actual modelling.
I'd take a quiet stretch next. Not optimistic.
Solidarity. Bring snacks.
I'll bring the good ones if you promise not to talk about backfills.
No deal
Since neither of our tickets covers it — do you want to do the recommender eval with me? Nobody else is going to.
Yes. It's the more interesting half of this sprint anyway.
Cold-start model is roughed in and pushed — that was the two of us at one screen all afternoon. The fallback stops firing on everyone now.
